correctness.rationale: The normalized unit-modulus three-by-three determinant rigidity argument is reconstructed. Its modular specialization yields exact rank conditions. Fine/coarse congruence classes yield B1,B2,B3 after explicit overlap subtraction; the p-adic ultrametric property partitions every row triple into E or I type. The rank-one closed expression follows from a finite geometric sum of Q_v. These cover every prime p>=2 and integer k>=2, including boundary p=2,k=2. The actual embedded Python checker exactly evaluates cyclotomic ranks exhaustively at six orders and checks 36,000 seeded cases at four other orders, independently matching local and global predictions. No finite extrapolation is invoked.

value.rationale: The all-depth exact rank multiplicities are a canonical arithmetic interpolation invariant, extend a depth-two census to infinitely many nontrivial prime powers, and distinguish rank-one from rank-two frequency of loss. The rank-one closed law shows depth-enhanced rare failure, with coefficient 1-p^-2 times k on the N^-2 scale. This resolves a natural complete classification rather than an arbitrary cutoff or a renamed theorem. No downstream theorem is required to motivate exact interpolation incidence.
